title: Affiliate Definition, Control Threshold, and Affiliate Status
where_to_look: Definitions of Affiliate and Control, plus Representative, Receiving Party, and permitted-disclosure provisions.
required: Define Affiliates by direct or indirect control, common control, and ownership of more than 50% of voting rights, with no automatic affiliate obligations.
fallback: Accept a majority-control Affiliate definition, but retain the rule that an Affiliate is bound only after receiving Confidential Information from or at a Party’s direction.
escalate_if: Escalate any definition based on partial ownership or any term making Affiliates parties, representatives, or obligors without receipt of Confidential Information.
flag_if: Affiliate status is triggered by any ownership interest without a control threshold.
Control is undefined or uses less than majority voting rights.
The definition is limited to wholly owned subsidiaries or direct control.
Affiliates are automatically treated as Representatives, agents, Receiving Parties, or obligors.
Affiliate obligations apply without receipt of Confidential Information from or at a Party’s direction.
preferred_language: “Affiliate” means any person or entity that directly or indirectly Controls, is Controlled by, or is under common Control with a Party, where “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities or voting power of the applicable entity. No Affiliate shall be deemed a Party’s Representative or agent, or have any obligation under this Agreement, unless it receives Confidential Information from or at the direction of that Party.
confidence_note: Based on 21 findings across multiple counterparties, consistent direction toward a majority-voting control threshold and no automatic affiliate obligations.

title: Representative Disclosure and Flow-Down Confidentiality
where_to_look: Review permitted-disclosure, Representative, agent and employee, affiliate, and third-party assistance provisions.
required: Require disclosure only to need-to-know Representatives who receive confidentiality notice and no-less-restrictive duties, with party responsibility for breaches.
fallback: Accept substantially similar written or professional confidentiality obligations, provided notice and responsibility for Representative breaches remain.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause allowing disclosure without a need-to-know limit or confidentiality flow-down, or disclaiming responsibility for Representative breaches.
flag_if: The clause permits disclosure to Representatives without a need-to-know requirement.
The clause requires prior written consent for each Representative disclosure.
Representative obligations are less protective than the Agreement's confidentiality and non-use obligations.
The recipient need not inform Representatives of the confidential nature of the information.
The recipient is not responsible for breaches by its Representatives or downstream recipients.
preferred_language: A Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its Affiliates, employees, officers, directors, consultants, advisors, and other Representatives who need to know it for the Purpose, provided that the Receiving Party informs each Representative of the confidential nature of the information and requires each Representative to comply with written, professional, or other legally enforceable confidentiality and non-use obligations no less restrictive than those contained in this Agreement. The Receiving Party remains responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its Representatives.
confidence_note: Based on 24 findings across multiple counterparties, the direction is consistent toward confidentiality notice, no-less-restrictive flow-down obligations, and responsibility for Representative breaches.

title: Confidential Information Protection Standard and Security Procedures
where_to_look: Review confidentiality obligations, information-security procedures, and representative-access provisions.
required: Require care for the recipient’s own information of like importance, with a reasonable-care floor and advance-written security procedures.
fallback: Accept an express reasonable-care standard and security procedures provided in writing before access, without requiring agreement to each procedure.
escalate_if: Escalate any strict-liability security obligation or any requirement to follow security procedures not provided in advance.
flag_if: The clause measures protection only against the recipient’s treatment of its own information.
The clause lacks an express minimum standard of reasonable care.
The clause requires compliance with security procedures without advance written notice.
The clause requires the recipient to agree to security procedures before access.
The clause imposes liability for unauthorized access without regard to the responsible party’s fault.
preferred_language: Recipient shall protect Discloser’s Confidential Information using the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of like importance, provided that such care shall be no less than reasonable care under the circumstances. Recipient shall comply with Discloser’s on-site, remote-access, and related security rules and procedures to the extent provided to Recipient in writing in advance.
confidence_note: Based on 13 findings across 12 counterparties, consistent direction toward a reasonable-care floor and recurring advance-written security procedures.

title: Independent-development exclusion and evidentiary requirements
where_to_look: Independent-development exclusions in the Confidential Information definition or exclusions paragraph.
required: Require Recipient to substantiate independent development without use, reference to, or direction from anyone with Confidential Information.
fallback: Accept a no-use-only exclusion only if Recipient bears the burden of proof and preserves contemporaneous written records.
escalate_if: Escalate before accepting any exclusion that permits independent-development claims after use, reference, or direction from an informed person.
flag_if: An independent-development exclusion appears in the confidentiality provisions.
The exclusion requires only that personnel lacked access to the information.
The exclusion omits reference to the Confidential Information.
The exclusion omits direction from a person with knowledge of the Confidential Information.
The clause contains no written-record or proof requirement.
preferred_language: Information independently developed by Recipient shall be excluded from Confidential Information only if Recipient demonstrates through contemporaneous written records that such information was developed without use of, reference to, or direction from any person who has knowledge of Confidential Information.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings across 3 counterparties, the movement toward a stricter independent-development exclusion is consistent, but only one finding was high significance.

title: Attorneys’ Fees and Enforcement-Cost Recovery
where_to_look: Look in attorneys’ fees, enforcement-cost, dispute-resolution, and arbitration provisions.
required: Require each party to bear its own fees and enforcement costs, with no automatic prevailing-party recovery.
fallback: Accept discretionary fee and cost awards by a court or arbitrator, but reject automatic prevailing-party shifting.
escalate_if: Escalate before accepting any clause requiring a defaulting or non-prevailing party to pay the other party’s fees or costs.
flag_if: The clause requires the non-prevailing party to pay the prevailing party’s attorneys’ fees.
The clause requires the defaulting party to reimburse enforcement costs.
The arbitration clause automatically shifts fees and costs to the non-prevailing party.
The clause permits recovery of fees incurred before suit is filed.
preferred_language: Each party shall bear its own attorneys’ fees, court costs, arbitration fees, and other enforcement expenses arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and no party shall recover those amounts from another party solely because it is the prevailing party.
confidence_note: Based on 2 findings, consistent direction toward eliminating automatic fee shifting, with discretionary awards retained in arbitration.

title: NDA Indemnity and Breach Cost Allocation
where_to_look: Review indemnification, hold-harmless, defense, breach-liability, and cost-recovery provisions.
required: Delete broad indemnity, defense, and hold-harmless obligations; limit breach liability to direct losses caused by a material breach.
fallback: Accept a narrow mutual indemnity limited to direct losses caused by a material breach, without a defense duty, affiliate expansion, or hold-harmless language.
escalate_if: Do not accept defense obligations, third-party indemnity, uncapped exposure, or affiliate or consultant liability beyond material breach without attorney approval.
flag_if: The clause requires a party to indemnify the other party.
The clause requires a party to hold the other party harmless.
The clause requires a party to defend the other party.
The clause imposes liability for breaches by affiliates or consultants.
The clause permits recovery without a material-breach threshold.
preferred_language: Each Party shall be liable only for losses directly caused by its own material breach of this Agreement or a material breach by its Affiliates or engaged consultants that received Confidential Information; neither Party shall be required to defend, indemnify, or hold harmless the other Party.
confidence_note: Based on 12 findings across 7 counterparties, the position is consistently to remove broad indemnity and limit recovery to direct losses from material breach.
matching_clause_names: Indemnification and Liability for Use of Information

title: Purpose, Business Relationship, and Permitted Use
where_to_look: Purpose or preamble recital and the permitted-use restriction for Confidential Information.
required: Define a specific business purpose and limit use to evaluating, discussing, and pursuing that relationship.
fallback: Accept a potential-business-relationship purpose if use remains limited to that relationship and other uses require written authorization.
escalate_if: Escalate any unrestricted operational, manufacturing, commercial, affiliate, or future-agreement use of Confidential Information.
flag_if: The Purpose is blank or does not identify the project, transaction, products, services, or relationship.
Permitted-use language allows use beyond the stated business relationship.
The clause permits performance of a future agreement without express written authorization.
The Purpose extends to unidentified affiliates or third parties.
The restriction permits manufacturing, commercialization, or operational use of Confidential Information.
preferred_language: Each Receiving Party shall use Confidential Information solely to evaluate, discuss, and pursue the parties’ potential business relationship concerning the [identified project or transaction], and for no other purpose. A Receiving Party may use Confidential Information to perform a subsequent written agreement only to the extent that agreement expressly authorizes such use in writing.
confidence_note: Based on 15 findings across 15 counterparties, the direction toward a defined purpose and purpose-limited use is consistent, while treatment of later performance and relationship breadth is mixed.
matching_clause_names: Permitted Use / Information and Ideas Restriction

title: Waiver and Preservation of Rights
where_to_look: Waiver, No Waiver, and General Contract Administration provisions.
required: Require mutual preservation of rights after failure, delay, or omission, with waivers effective only in signed writing by the waiving Party.
fallback: Accept mutual no-waiver protection for failure or delay and a signed-writing requirement, even if omission or acquiescence is not addressed.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that permits waiver through silence, delay, course of dealing, or conduct, or without authorized written approval.
flag_if: The no-waiver protection applies only to the Disclosing Party.
The clause treats a failure or delay in enforcement as a waiver.
A waiver can be effective without a writing signed by the waiving Party.
The clause allows acquiescence to arise from delay or omission.
The agreement contains no express preservation of rights after delayed enforcement.
preferred_language: No failure, delay, or omission by either Party in exercising any right, power, privilege, or remedy under this Agreement shall impair that right, power, privilege, or remedy, constitute a waiver of any default, or constitute acquiescence thereto, nor shall it preclude that Party from exercising any other right, power, privilege, or remedy. No waiver shall be effective unless set forth in a writing signed by an authorized representative of the Party giving the waiver.
confidence_note: Based on 7 findings across 3 counterparties, the direction is consistent, with all changes rated medium significance.

title: No Partnership, Agency, Obligation to Transact, or Obligation to Disclose
where_to_look: Look in No Partnership, No Agency, No Obligation to Disclose, or Further Agreements provisions.
required: Require a reciprocal disclaimer of agency, partnership, joint venture, teaming, further contracting, business relationships, and disclosure obligations.
fallback: Accept a reciprocal no-agency and no-partnership disclaimer with no duty to disclose particular Confidential Information or enter further agreements.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that creates or implies a duty to transact, form a business relationship, act as an agent, or disclose information.
flag_if: The agreement describes the parties as agents, partners, joint venturers, or teaming parties.
The agreement obligates either party to enter a future contract, subcontract, or business relationship.
The agreement requires either party to disclose particular Confidential Information.
The disclaimer applies to only one party.
preferred_language: Nothing in this Agreement creates or shall be construed to create any agency, partnership, joint venture, teaming arrangement, or other business relationship between the Parties. Neither Party is obligated to enter into any further agreement, contract, subcontract, or other transaction with the other Party. No Party is required by this Agreement to disclose any particular Confidential Information to any other Party.
confidence_note: Based on 6 underlying negotiated positions across 6 counterparties, the direction is consistent, with one service-related disclosure carveout.

title: Severability, Integration, and Conflicts with Other Agreements
where_to_look: Review the severability, entire-agreement, order-of-precedence, and conflicts-with-other-agreements provisions.
required: Require minimum reformation and a narrow integration rule that preserves other written agreements.
fallback: Accept standard severability and a conflict rule limited to this Agreement’s subject matter without blanket supersession.
escalate_if: Escalate any blanket precedence rule or language that supersedes, amends, or releases obligations under another agreement.
flag_if: The agreement states that it supersedes all prior or existing agreements.
The agreement gives itself precedence over every other agreement between the parties.
The agreement lacks severability or minimum-reformation language.
The agreement does not preserve obligations under other written agreements.
A later written confidentiality agreement is not given priority over this agreement.
preferred_language: If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect, and the affected provision shall be enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law or reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties regarding its subject matter and is in addition to, and does not supersede, amend, modify, limit, or restrict, any other written agreement between the Parties. If a conflict concerns confidentiality, the more restrictive obligation applies, and a subsequent written agreement signed by both Parties that expressly addresses confidentiality controls to the extent of the conflict.
confidence_note: Based on 10 findings across 9 counterparties, the severability direction is consistent but integration and conflict treatment is mixed.

title: Notices, Delivery Methods, and Deemed Receipt
where_to_look: Notices clause and any notice-address or delivery-method provision.
required: Require complete notice contacts, confirmed electronic delivery, refusal-as-receipt, and five-business-day mail receipt.
fallback: Accept a three-business-day mail period if notice contacts are complete, electronic receipt is confirmed, and refusal counts as receipt.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision that deems electronic notice effective solely upon transmission.
flag_if: The notice clause permits email or facsimile delivery.
The notice clause lacks confirmed-delivery language for electronic notices.
The notice clause sets a mailed-notice period shorter than five business days.
The notice clause omits receipt or refusal of acceptance as a deemed-receipt event.
The notice section contains a blank or incomplete notice address or email contact.
preferred_language: Each party shall designate a complete notice address and email address in this Agreement. Notice shall be deemed given upon actual receipt or refusal of acceptance. Notice sent by email or facsimile shall be deemed given on the day transmitted if transmitted during the recipient’s normal business hours and receipt is confirmed, and on the next business day if transmitted after those hours and receipt is confirmed. Notice sent by registered or certified mail, postage prepaid, shall be deemed given five business days after deposit with the U.S. Postal Service.
confidence_note: Based on 25 listed findings across 11 counterparties, the delivery-method direction is consistent, with significance predominantly medium.

title: Purpose-Limited Use and No Broad Circumvention Restraints
where_to_look: Use and Disclosure, Restricted Use, Non-Circumvention, and related business-activity restriction clauses.
required: Require mutual, Purpose-only use and disclosure limits and delete broad non-circumvention, non-solicitation, and business-interference restraints.
fallback: Accept a mutual, time-limited non-circumvention restriction tied solely to misuse of Confidential Information involving identified contacts.
escalate_if: Escalate before accepting any restriction that bars ordinary business contacts or independent development, or that is unilateral, indefinite, or untethered to Confidential Information.
flag_if: Use is permitted for a later agreement or for purposes beyond the defined Purpose.
Disclosure is allowed without an express exception in the agreement.
A party is barred from contacting or pursuing business with persons identified through Confidential Information.
The NDA restricts employee solicitation or dealings with suppliers, distributors, or customers.
The clause lacks a safe harbor for independently possessed or independently developed information.
preferred_language: Each Party shall use Confidential Information received from the other Party solely for the Purpose and shall disclose it only as expressly permitted by this Agreement. This Agreement does not restrict either Party’s use of information independently possessed or independently developed without use of the other Party’s Confidential Information, or ordinary business activities that do not use or disclose the other Party’s Confidential Information. This Agreement imposes no non-circumvention, non-solicitation, or supplier, distributor, or customer non-interference obligation.
confidence_note: Based on 14 findings across 11 counterparties, strong direction favors mutual, Purpose-limited use and removal of broad circumvention restraints, with a narrow consent-based exception.
